title: 2025 World Cup Carmel: Hubert Kos Clinches US Open 50 Back Record
content: At the 2025 World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Hungarian Olympic champion Hubert Kos won the men's 50m backstroke final with a time of 22.65 seconds, setting a new U.S. Open record. This performance surpassed the previous U.S. Open record of 22.72, set by Dylan Carter in 2022. Kos' time was just 0.01 seconds shy of his own Hungarian national record of 22.64, set at the 2024 Short Course World Championships. Romania's Ralf Tribuntsov finished second with a time of 22.91, and Trinidad & Tobago's Dylan Carter claimed bronze with a time of 23.00. The world record in the event remains 22.11, set by Russia's Kliment Kolesnikov in 2022, while the world junior record is 22.47, held by Russia's Miron Lifintsev (2024), and the World Cup record is 22.58, set by Australia's Isaac Cooper (2024). The event took place from October 10–12, 2025, at the SCM (25-meter) pool in Carmel, Indiana.

title: Swimming World Cup: Pioggia Di Record Nella Seconda Serata Di Finali A Carmel
content: The second day of the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, became a celebration of speed, with four new records set—spanning world, American, and national records. Australian swimmer Mollie O'Callaghan set a new U.S. Open Record in the women’s 200-meter freestyle with a time of 1:50.77, surpassing Siobhan Haughey’s previous mark of 1:51.99 and becoming the third-fastest performer in history, behind only Haughey (1:50.31) and Sarah Sjöström (1:50.42). In the men’s 200-meter individual medley, Shaine Casas improved his own American and U.S. Open Record to 1:49.43, eight hundredths of a second faster than his time at the 2024 Short Course Worlds, and narrowly defeated Léon Marchand. Casas had already set a U.S. Open Record in the 100-meter individual medley the previous day (50.86), confirming his elite form. In the women’s 100-meter breaststroke, Germany’s Anna Elendt set a new national record of 1:03.83, improving her previous best of 1:04.05 from the 2022 World Championships. The gold went to American Kate Douglass (1:02.90), with Estonia’s Eneli Jefimova (1:03.35) second. Elendt now holds all German records in breaststroke (50, 100, and 200 meters) in both long and short course. In the men’s 50-meter breaststroke, Netherlands’ Caspar Corbeau set a new national record of 25.78, placing him among the top ten European performers of all time. He finished just three hundredths of a second behind South Africa’s Chris Smith (25.75), with Belarus’ Ilya Shymanovich third in 25.79, marking a high-level final. The event highlighted the depth of international swimming talent.

title: Hubert Kos crushes U.S. Open Record, Leon Marchand cracks French Record in 200 back
content: At the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Hubert Kos shattered the U.S. Open record in the men's 200-meter backstroke with a time of 1:46.84, the second-fastest swim of his career, winning the event. His teammate Leon Marchand finished second in 1:47.68, a personal best and a new French record, nearly one second faster than the previous national mark. Marchand, who had not previously swum the event at elite level, led early with a 25.03 first 50 and a 52.60 split, but Kos pulled away with a 26.46 final 50—the fastest in the field by nearly a second. Shaine Casas, also from Texas, took third in 1:49.81, the only other swimmer under 1:50, and later set a new U.S. Open record in the 100 IM. Kos’s time ranks as the second-fastest in history, while Marchand now stands as the 10th-fastest man ever in the event. The previous U.S. Open record of 1:48.40, held by Casas since 2022, was surpassed by both Kos and Marchand. Marchand’s performance marked his first elite-level appearance in the 200 backstroke, and he now holds world, Olympic, NCAA, or national records in all other 200-meter events except this one.

title: Daniele Del Signore Campione Del Mondo Jr E Record Italiano Di Categoria Nei 50 Dorso
content: Daniele Del Signore captured the gold medal in the men's 50‑meter backstroke at the 2025 World Junior Swimming Championships in Otopeni, Romania, clocking 24.91 seconds. The time broke the 25‑second barrier, making him the first Italian junior swimmer to do so. He shared the podium with silver medalist Georgii Iakovlev, who matched the same time, and bronze medalist John Shortt, who finished 25.06 seconds, just 0.15 seconds behind. Del Signore’s performance also lowered his own Italian junior record from 25.02 seconds, set the previous day, to 24.91 seconds. The world record for the event is 23.55 seconds by Kliment Kolesnikov (RUS), the world junior record is 24.00 seconds by the same swimmer, and the championship record is 24.44 seconds by Ksawery Masiuk (POL).

title: McKeown Nabs 1:58.86 200 Back PB En Route To Carmel Gold
content: At the 2025 World Aquatics Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Australian Olympic champion Kaylee McKeown set a new personal best of 1:58.86 in the women's 200m backstroke, becoming the second-fastest swimmer of all time in the event. Her time, achieved in a 25-meter short course pool, broke the 2:00 barrier and surpassed her previous PB of 1:59.26 from the 2022 Short Course World Championships. McKeown’s performance established a new Australian national record and a new Oceanian record. American Olympic medalist Regan Smith finished second in 2:00.07, while teammate Charlottee Crush placed third in 2:02.28. Smith holds the current world record of 1:58.04, set at the 2024 Short Course World Championships. The event took place on October 12, 2025, as part of the SCM (short course meters) competition.

title: Shaine Casas Breaks His First Career Individual American Record in the 200 IM
content: American swimmer Shaine Casas broke his first individual American record and second U.S. Open Record in the 200-meter individual medley (IM) at the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, on October 12, 2025. Competing in short course meters (SCM), Casas clocked a time of 1:49.43, shaving 0.08 seconds off his previous best from the December 2024 World Short Course Championships and surpassing the prior U.S. Open Record of 1:50.76 set by Japan’s Daiya Seto in 2019. His performance made him the fastest swimmer of any nationality on American soil. Despite being approximately half a second slower on the breaststroke leg compared to his December 2024 race, Casas made up ground on the freestyle leg, outsplit defending Olympic 200-meter breaststroke champion Leon Marchand on that segment and led wire-to-wire. This victory marks Casas’ first individual American record and follows his earlier U.S. Open Record in the 100 IM (50.86) on Friday evening.

title: Natação Adaptada: Marco Meneses foi 6.º na final dos 100 metros costas
content: Marco Meneses finished sixth in the final of the 100‑metre backstroke S11 event at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore. He had qualified fourth in the heats with a time of 1:10.03 and improved to 1:09.95 in the final. The race was won by Spain’s Albert Gelis, who set a new world record of 1:05.14. Meneses had previously placed seventh in the 200‑metre freestyle final and missed the 50‑metre freestyle final by 0.17 seconds. He will compete in the 400‑metre freestyle on Saturday.

title: Impone leonesa Celia Pulido 2 nuevos récords mexicanos en natación - Quadratín
content: Celia Pulido, a swimmer from León, Guanajuato, set two new Mexican national records in swimming at the 2025 World Cup Swimming Carmel event held this weekend in Indiana, United States. She broke the 26-second barrier in the 50-meter backstroke with a time of 25.83 seconds, placing her fourth globally—just one-hundredth of a second short of the podium. In a high-level final, she was surpassed by Kaylee McKeown (25.42 seconds), Mollie O'Callaghan (25.80), and Katharine Berkoff (25.82), with Pulido finishing just 0.01 seconds behind the bronze medalist. Her performance marked a historic achievement for Mexican swimming, showcasing determination, talent, and Leonese pride.

title: Corbeau Sets New U.S. Open Record, Marchand Resets French Record in the 200 Breaststroke
content: At the 2025 Swimming World Cup in Carmel, Indiana, Caspar Corbeau set a new U.S. Open Record in the men's 200-meter breaststroke with a time of 2:01.63, winning gold and securing his second victory of the meet after also winning the 100 breaststroke. His time surpassed Cody Miller's previous U.S. Open Record of 2:02.33 from the 2015 Duel in the Pool, though it fell 0.20 seconds short of Arno Kamminga's Dutch Record of 2:01.43 set in 2020. Corbeau had previously set a national record in the 50-meter breaststroke with a time of 25.78 earlier in the meet. Leon Marchand, the defending Olympic champion in the long-course version of the event, finished second with a time of 2:02.00, improving his own French Record from 2:02.99 (set October 2024). Despite being slightly off-form, Marchand's performance marked a new personal best and national record. The event was held in short course meters (SCM) at the Carmel, Indiana venue from October 10–12, 2025.

title: John Shortt makes 50m backstroke final at World Junior Championships
content: John Shortt, an 18‑year‑old swimmer from Galway, qualified for the 50m backstroke final at the World Junior Championships in Romania by recording a time of '25.36' in the semi‑final, placing seventh overall. He improved his time by over a second from the morning heat. The fastest qualifier was Russian Georgii Iakovlev with '24.58', followed by Italy’s Daniele Del Signore ('25.02') and Australia’s Henry Allan ('25.05'). Shortt had previously won gold in the 100m backstroke and added a European junior title in that event the week before. The 50m backstroke final is scheduled for Friday at 4:20 pm Irish time.
